questions.q: State the formula for kinetic energy of an object of mass \( m \) moving with speed \( v \), and give its SI unit.
questions.a: \( KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \); SI unit is joule (J). A wrong answer like \( KE = mv \) or unit as newton reveals the student confuses momentum with kinetic energy or force with energy.

questions.q: Why does the kinetic energy formula have a factor of \( \frac{1}{2} \) and \( v^2 \) instead of just \( mv \) or \( mv^2 \)?
questions.a: The \( \frac{1}{2} \) arises from the integration of \( F\,ds \) using \( v^2 = u^2 + 2as \) (or average velocity \( v/2 \) during acceleration from rest). The \( v^2 \) comes from the kinematic relation linking displacement to velocity squared. A student answering "because energy is proportional to \( v^2 \)" without deriving shows they memorized but don't understand the work-energy link.

questions.q: A 150 g cricket ball is bowled at 144 km/h. Calculate its kinetic energy in joules.
questions.a:
Step 1: Convert mass to kg: \( 150 \, \text{g} = 0.150 \, \text{kg} \).  
Step 2: Convert speed to m/s: \( 144 \, \text{km/h} = 144 \times \frac{1000}{3600} = 40 \, \text{m/s} \).  
Step 3: Use \( KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.150 \times (40)^2 \).  
Step 4: \( KE = 0.075 \times 1600 = 120 \, \text{J} \).  
Step 5: Check: a fast cricket ball has energy ~100 J — reasonable.  
Wrong unit conversion (using km/h directly) gives 432,000 J — reveals ignoring SI unit consistency.

questions.q: Two trucks have the same kinetic energy. Truck A has mass 4000 kg, Truck B has mass 1000 kg. Compare their speeds and momenta.
questions.a:
\( KE_A = KE_B \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}m_A v_A^2 = \frac{1}{2}m_B v_B^2 \Rightarrow v_A/v_B = \sqrt{m_B/m_A} = \sqrt{1000/4000} = 1/2 \). So \( v_B = 2v_A \).  
Momentum \( p = mv \): \( p_A = 4000 v_A \), \( p_B = 1000 \times 2v_A = 2000 v_A \). Thus \( p_A = 2p_B \).  
A student saying speeds are equal or momenta are equal confuses kinetic energy with momentum or ignores the square root relation.

questions.q: A student claims: "If a car's speed doubles, its kinetic energy doubles." Evaluate this statement and correct it if wrong.
questions.a: The statement is incorrect. Since \( KE \propto v^2 \), doubling speed (\( v \to 2v \)) makes kinetic energy increase by factor \( 2^2 = 4 \). The student likely thinks kinetic energy is directly proportional to velocity (like momentum). This reveals a confusion between linear and quadratic dependence.

questions.q: Design a simple classroom experiment using a ramp, a toy car, and a measuring tape to show that kinetic energy is proportional to \( v^2 \), not \( v \).
questions.a: Release the car from different heights \( h \) on the ramp. Measure speed \( v \) at bottom (using time over fixed distance). Plot \( KE \) (calculated from \( mgh \)) vs \( v \) and vs \( v^2 \). The \( KE \) vs \( v^2 \) graph will be linear through origin. A poor answer suggests measuring only one height or plotting \( KE \) vs \( v \) and claiming linearity — shows lack of experimental design understanding.
